title: Contrarian growth habits & manager-priming notebook
content:
Purpose: quick, noisy scratchpad for preparing manager syncs, crystallizing small behavior experiments, and keeping a rolling evidence log for performance conversations. This is intentionally fuzzy — the goal is to capture patterns, not produce a polished narrative.

Topline goals (3):
- Grow influence on hiring decisions in Q4: push for clearer rubric adoption on interviewing panels. Measure: 4 panels where rubric used + 2 hiring decisions with explicit rubric notes.
- Run 2 micro-experiments that reduce candidate time-to-offer by 10% without sacrificing slate quality. Current baseline: 14 days offer lead time.
- Improve cross-functional trust: host 3 short calibration walk-throughs with Eng, Product, and SRE to reduce escalations about compensation/hours.

Micro habits I want to try (2-week experiments):
- 10-minute "post-interview triage" note within 2 hours. Short format: 1 line candidate signal, 1 line risk, 1 line call-to-action for panel. Track adherence in spreadsheet.
- One weekly 15-min office hours with a rotating team (Eng/Prod/Design) for quick compensation questions. Put on calendar as recurring stub.

Evidence snippets (for manager + calibration):
- Sep 18: nudged hiring manager on rubric after interview. Manager agreed to add rubric item to next debrief; saved one rework of interview loop.
- Oct 02: flagged slower offer pipeline at final interview stage — TA routed candidate back to hiring manager, offer made in 9 days (benchmark improved).
- Nov 21: ran a 10-minute calibration with infra leads; clarified how we weight internal vs external candidates; one decision changed accordingly.

Manager sync cheat sheet (scripts + cues):
- Opening (30s): "Two quick things I want to run today — one signals update and one low-friction ask. I’ll keep it <10 mins unless we want to expand."
- Evidence-first ask pattern: 1) Quick data point (1 sentence), 2) Impact / risk (1 sentence), 3) Specific ask (one action + owner + timeframe).
- Pushback framing: "If we don't do X now, we expect Y delay; if we do X it's likely to save Z cycles and reduce candidate drop-off."
- Calibration cue to surface: "I want your read on tradeoffs between speed and panel completeness for senior IC hiring — do we prioritize speed or standard panel?"

Self-review primitives (how I'll assemble quarter narrative):
- Metric anchors: time-to-offer, % panels using rubric, candidate NPS (where available), number of escalations resolved.
- Story fragments to collect: 1) Example of a hire that benefitted from rubric. 2) Small operational win (e.g., reduced offer time). 3) A counterexample where we erred — what I learned.
- Evidence format: one-line summary + link (Jira/convo) + date. Keep 10 most recent positive and 3 learning moments.

Sample micro-asks to raise in 1:1s (pick one per sync):
- "Could you back a one-time budget to pilot 2-day paid recruiting test assignments for senior candidates? I think it will improve match quality and reduce churn."
- "Can we lock a band exception for candidate X? I’ll follow with the evidence packet and a quick calibration note."
- "Can you join a 15-min calibration with Eng next week? We want to align on rubric enforcement."

Handling tricky feedback (phrases and mental models):
- When told 'process is too heavy' -> reframe: "Which exact step felt heavy? If we can cut X without increasing risk, I will."
- When manager dodges a request -> use "implementation friction" test: "What's the smallest piece you can approve this week?"

Risks I'm tracking (and mitigations):
- Risk: rubber-stamping hires to expedite. Mitigation: require one asynchronous rubric check before offer for senior roles.
- Risk: burnout from too many ad-hoc calibration meetings. Mitigation: convert to 15-min standing blocks and rotate representatives.

Coachable moments I want to capture this quarter:
- How I escalate when a hiring manager won't follow basic steps — I want to be assertive but preserve relationship. Note to self: practice scripts.
- How I prioritize competing asks from three executives — want a principled triage lens: impact / time-to-value / downstream ops cost.

Quick scripts to rehearse (out loud):
- Asking for time: "Can you spare 15 minutes this week for a quick calibration? I can come with a 1-slide summary and a proposed decision."
- Push for rubric usage: "I noticed the panel missed rubric item Y; can we add it to this panel's sync and retroactively score? It'll help us avoid mismatch."

Open questions for manager: (use as prompting in sync)
- Which metric would you prioritize if you had to pick one to evaluate my impact this quarter?
- How do you want me to escalate when a hiring manager persistently ignores the rubric?
- Any small leadership moments you think I should try to own in the next month?

Next actions (in the next 7 days):
- Draft a one-pager that proposes the 2 micro-experiments (time-to-offer + paid test assignment). Attach rough budget and measurement plan. (Due: 2026-02-16)
- Put 3 short evidence entries into the 'quarter narrative' doc (link in linked_artifacts) for manager review.
- Book 2 office hours slots with Eng leads and Product leads.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep language concise in the manager packet; they are time-limited. Use 3-line evidence bullets.
- Celebrate small wins publicly (one Slack post per small win) to build momentum across teams.
- If an ask stalls for >10 days, escalate with a single data point and a suggested next step.

Versioning and signals:
- This doc = working scratchpad. Every time I prepare for a manager sync I will copy the top chunk to a dated note: "mgr-sync-YYYYMMDD" and record the outcome. That creates an audit trail.

End of scratchpad.
